# Cross-examination, job 4 of 4: the plain-words file against the results

## (a) Objections

| id | place | objection | what shows it | the exact fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X4.1 | `S111/3 plain words.md`, §3 last paragraph ("close to what the rates alone lead one to expect"), root in §2 | The plain file never mentions the second kind of change: at each split the world also, with probability 0.05 each, inserts one random instruction or deletes one. Without it the fidelity claim is wrong — from the copying-mistake rates alone one expects about 78 in 100 exact copies at the low rate, not the 69 reported, so they are *not* "close to what the rates alone lead one to expect". The results' expectation is (1 − rate)^100 × 0.95 × 0.95, the 0.95s being exactly the insert and delete chances. | `S111/2 ...md` §1: "one inserted and one deleted instruction each with probability 0.05 per birth"; §2 C3: "'Expected' is (1 − rate)^100 × 0.95 × 0.95"; `runs/configuration/avida.cfg` lines 63–64: "DIVIDE_INS_PROB 0.05", "DIVIDE_DEL_PROB 0.05". | In §2, after the copying-mistake sentence, add: "At each split the world also, one time in twenty each, adds one random instruction to the copy or takes one away." In §3 change "close to what the rates alone lead one to expect" to "close to what those rates, together with the one-in-twenty added and removed instructions, lead one to expect". |
| X4.2 | §4, second part ("With the copying mistakes switched off entirely, nothing changed at all") | The no-change control (K5) switched off all three kinds of change, not just copying mistakes; with only copy errors off, the one-in-twenty insertions and deletions would still change the programs. The sentence misstates what the control shows. | `runs/the exact commands.txt`, control_K5 line: "-set COPY_MUT_PROB 0 -set DIVIDE_INS_PROB 0 -set DIVIDE_DEL_PROB 0"; `S111/2 ...md` §7 item 4/K5, and `runs/the worlds over time.md` K5 row. | "With every kind of change switched off — the copying mistakes and the added and removed instructions — nothing changed at all: after 5,000 time steps all 3,600 programs were still the first program." |
| X4.3 | §1, "Remains" bullet ("a program that cannot copy itself also remains, for as long as you like, in a world where nothing dies of old age") | "For as long as you like" is stronger than the results: the control ran 2,000 updates and the program remained through them; nothing longer was run. §5 of the same file states it correctly. | `S111/2 ...md` §4 controls: "K3: ... remained for the whole 2,000 updates"; `runs/the worlds over time.md`: "control_K3 ... last_update_with_organisms: 2000". | "And a program that cannot copy itself also remains — in its control it stayed for all 2,000 time steps — in a world where nothing dies of old age." |
| X4.4 | §7, departures ("The first try of four control runs failed from a missing line break in a file and was run again") | Not what the results say: three controls (K2, K3, K4) failed from the missing line break; the fourth (K1) did not fail but ran wrongly, without the switch-off instruction defined; and all five controls were rerun, not four. | `S111/2 ...md` §7 item 5: "the first attempt of K2, K3 and K4 failed at once ... and K1 ran without `nop-X` defined; nothing from that attempt is used. Fixed in the scripts, and all five controls rerun." | "The first try of the control runs went wrong — three stopped at once from a missing line break in a file, and the fourth ran without the switch-off instruction in it; nothing from that try was used, and all five controls were run again." |
| X4.5 | §3, example ("Switch off the 'copy one instruction' step, and the program runs, makes room, and never fills it: no copy") | The mechanism story ("runs, makes room, and never fills it") was not measured and is not in the results; the results state only that this knockout stops exact self-copying. It reads as an observation. | `S111/2 ...md` §2 C2 and `runs/copying and knockouts.md`: only "knockout leaves self-copying..." / "15 of 100 sites"; no run-and-room observation. | "Switch off the 'copy one instruction' step — the one step that does the copying — and no copy is made." |
| X4.6 | §2 ("the world writes a random instruction instead: a **copying mistake**") | "Instead" says the instruction is always a different one; the results and the build notes say the random draw can produce the same instruction again (it matters to the expected-fidelity range). | `S111/2 ...md` §2 C3: "the upper if an error can redraw the same one (it can: `source/cpu/cInstSet.cc` 83-88)"; `runs/build notes ...md`, the copy-error row. | "Sometimes, when an instruction is copied, the world writes in a random instruction, which can even be the same one again: a **copying mistake**." |
| X4.7 | §1 ("about 6,300 to 16,000 generations") beside §5 ("over 6,300 to 15,900 generations"); §6 ("the simplest sum, NOT") | Two roundings of one number (15,940) in the same file, one of them (16,000) the coarser; and "the simplest sum" for NOT is not in the results, which state only "the hardest, EQU". | `S111/2 ...md` §2 C4: "6,310 to 15,940"; §5: "EQU (the hardest ...)"; nothing calls NOT the simplest. | Use "about 6,300 to 15,900 generations" in both places; in §6 write "For the sum NOT, about a fifth of the programs still did it afterwards (up to 46% in one run)." |

## (b) Checked, no objection

All other numbers and statements: §1 (100 instructions, ~3,600 by 1,000 steps, nine runs, 50,000 steps, EQU in six of nine, 15/85 split, 10,000 random programs); §2 (60×60 grid of 3,600, rates 1/400, 1/133, 1/50, 5+86+9, 389 steps); §3 (69/40/13 per 100, K1 66, K2 65); §4 (69–79% and 21–31%, 14–19% low and 27–36% high neutral with every high-rate run above every low-rate run, "survival of the flattest" hedge, shorter high-rate genomes, 84%/18%, every run at all six moments, copy loop gone by 20,000 in all six low and usual runs, two-or-three-instruction loops, no repairing instruction); §5 (never fewer than 3,481, no identical program, 0% to 49% copy loop at high, 58–84%, 65–86%, about a third, K3 2,000, K4 gone by 500); §6 (Marletto quote verbatim, 26 instructions, drop of 1.4 points and 44 of 3,600 consistent with the tables, 0.2–1.4 points, 1%–4%, 93–100%, 19–26, NOT about a fifth up to 46%); §7 tested/not-tested/unsure lists match the results' §7; §8 and §9. Terminology one-word-per-thing (program, world, copy, place, time step, switch off, sums, first program, test computer); "instruction" and "sums" used in the §1 summary before their §2/§6 definitions, as plain file 110 does with its own terms. S23: no removed word in Claude's own sentences (searched); no "model" (S43); nothing settled (S28: "Nothing here settles it", §8 "nothing is settled"); nothing chosen for the owner (S21: "yours to say", "yours to choose"); marked as written before the GLM check; starts with what happened and what it means; one next step at the end; style matches plain file 110.

## (c) Not reached

- The exact count "44 of the 3,600" for the dominant of the low-rate run in §6: per-run dominant counts are not in the summary tables (the results give only "5 to 44"), and the raw population files are not in this folder; the figure is consistent with the 1.4-point drop but could only be settled by rerunning the Marletto script or reading its raw output.
- Whether every number in the summary tables matches the raw runs: Avida's raw output is not here; I checked the plain file against the results, the `.json` and the tables only (job 2's angle).
- Whether Avida's rules are as the build notes read them from the source: no source in this folder (jobs 2 and 3).

END OF REPORT
